data.name: Narottam
data.gender_notes: Narottam is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Naro means ‘man’ or ‘people’. Tama means ‘delight’ or ‘joy’. Narottam is a name for a person who brings happiness and joy to the people. The name Narottam carries the meaning “Lord of the People” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Narottam usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the people and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that signifies the divine presence within, bringing joy and happiness to all.
data.etymology: Narottam belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the People.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Narottam total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Narottam has deep cultural signification in Hinduism as it represents the qualities of a righteous leader. One who brings happiness and joy to his people is highly respected. This name is commonly used in India and Nepal, particularly among the Vaishnavite community.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Narottam symbolizes living a joyful and content life. It also represents the attainment of self-realization and inner happiness, which ultimately leads to the joy and happiness of the people around us. The name is an inspiration to seek inner happiness and inner peace while also serving the people with kindness, compassion, and love.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Narottam: Radiant in divine wisdom and virtues. A beacon of pure consciousness and enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: Narottam was a renowned Jain scholar and writer during the 16th century in India. He was the founder of the Shvetambar Digambara Terapanth sect of Jainism.
historical_references.context: Religious leader and founder of a sect

historical_references.reference: Narottam was also a great Rajasthani poet and has contributed significantly to the Rajasthani literature through his works like 'Nagaraka Chandrak'.
